thread:
alex: Customer acme-inc reports monthly credits dropped to 0 immediately after they downgraded their plan at 2024-11-05T21:12:07Z. They expected proration to leave them with ~100k tokens but got 429s starting 2024-11-05T21:25Z. tenant=tenant_az42. Any quick triage?
priya: Do we have the billing event and any active streams? :thinking:
sam: @alex can you paste the ledger/plans event id and a snippet of the API errors?
alex: Billing event id bill_ev_9945 shows plan change at 2024-11-05T21:12:09Z. There was a websocket stream open from ~20:50Z. Logs show a big token bump then 429s. Snippet:
```
2024-11-05T21:23:15Z INFO tokens_consumed=2103450 session=ws://stream/tenant_az42
2024-11-05T21:25:02Z ERROR quota=0 enforcement=429 route=/v1/generate
```
sam: Two hypotheses: (1) our proration job calculates new allowance immediately but a race with active sessions attributes usage differently; (2) quota-service read stale usage from a read-replica then wrote a zero allowance. infra-oncall, any infra anomalies?
infra-oncall: We observed quota-sync-worker retrying against a read-replica at 21:11 which had ~90s replication lag after a failover. The worker retried and reconciled based on stale usage, then primary reconcile later corrected it at ~21:24. There was a late write that temporarily set visible quota to 0.
billing: Confirmed plan change recorded. Prorated_allowance calculation returned expected 100000, but ledger showed an interim negative balance entry from streaming usage that was only visible to primary. Replica read missed it, leading to a reconciliation mismatch. Pulling ledger entries now.
alex: Customer sees console 0/0 screenshot and is upset. They want to know if credits will be restored or if they need a manual top-up.
priya: For immediate remediation we can run a force reconcile for that tenant to recompute allowance from the canonical ledger. Repro steps for eng to validate: 1) create tenant with 3M monthly tokens; 2) start long-running streaming session consuming ~2M tokens; 3) issue plan downgrade API call; 4) observe quota-service reconciliation behavior and visible quota. Example API call to downgrade: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/downgrade -d '{"tenant":"tenant_az42","new_plan":"starter-100k"}'
```
sam: Quick mitigation: @billing can you run billing-prorate --tenant tenant_az42 --force-reconcile? That should recompute remaining allowance and patch visible quota. :pray:
billing: Done. Force reconcile executed at 2024-11-05T21:30:17Z. Console now shows 100000 tokens available and customer can resume. I'll append a note to the billing ticket for audit.
alex: Customer confirms services back to normal. They asked for root cause and whether this can happen to others.
infra-oncall: Root cause: short-lived replica lag during quota-sync created a race where reconcile used stale usage numbers and snapped visible quota to 0. Fixes: 1) hotfix to prefer primary reads for critical reconciles (merged), 2) guard that prevents snapshotting quota to 0 unless ledger confirms negative balance on both primary and replica, 3) add a canary regression for streaming+downgrade flow. Created INC-2024-774.
support-bot: FYI @channel we'll add a UI warning preventing immediate downgrades if active streaming token use > 20% of current allowance, and a background job to block plan-change until reconcile completes.
priya: We'll follow-up with an engineer-facing test and add an automated integration test that exercises streaming + plan change paths.
alex: I'll draft a customer-facing explanation + apology and include the manual fix we applied. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
